Sendgrid has always had that top-of-the-line experience... I've worked with them several times over the past 6 years sending 10 mil/month and 300k/month with zero issues. Inbound did have a hiccup with their SPF/DKIM checks though.

One thing Sendgrid is good at is letting people easily send emails on behalf of their clients while still passing SPF/DKIM checks, which Mailgun and Sparkpost make a bit harder. If you need to send on behalf of clients, Sendgrid is an obvious choice.

I've had some negative experiences working with SendGrid a few years ago, but honestly I think they've improved a great deal in the last couple of years. Some stuff still could use improvements (API, UI) but it felt a lot more stable and reliable last time I used it.
Mailgun is pretty slow to deliver emails, so I use SendGrid to send emails for [a login-link auth system] that's very sensitive to latency.
It's too bad SendGrid has struggled to get its marketing email solution off the ground in a meaningful way... their marketing solution brings in less than 20% of total revenue.

I've tried contacting sendgrid about phishing emails that look like they're from @sendgrid.com, using their own server. The SPF records match, so it isn't marked as junk mail... I sent it by mail, but yeah.. No reply.
My university straight up blocks any mail coming from a SendGrid IP because of the massive amount of phishing.

I got several emails with subject 'The following services failed to auto-renew and are about to expire' that I almost believed were real because they came from an actual sendgrid server. If SendGrid can't develop simple filters to deter phishing emails sent through their platform, they're going to end up with a lot of users being hacked.

I'm also a long-time (8+ year) Sendgrid user, and my accounts (one main account, 3 sub-accounts) were not put under review. I haven't needed customer support any time recently so I can't speak to that.
Super curious if you're evaluating options... the cost is astronomical when you go above 500,000 contacts.
I think they've simply continued going up market and care less about smaller players.
We switched to Postmark after they froze our account without notice. Best decision we made.
